title: 418. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Even and Odd Trigonometric Identities
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: State the identity for the cosine of a negative angle.
questions.question: For every angle \(\theta\), \(\cos(-\theta)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: The angles \(\theta\) and \(-\theta\) give unit-circle points that are reflections of each other in the \(x\)-axis, so they have the same \(x\)-coordinate. Hence \(\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta\); cosine is an even function.
questions.hint: Compare the unit-circle points for \(\theta\) and \(-\theta\); which coordinate do they share?

questions.learningObjective: State the identity for the sine of a negative angle.
questions.question: For every angle \(\theta\), \(\sin(-\theta)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Reflecting the unit-circle point for \(\theta\) in the \(x\)-axis gives the point for \(-\theta\), which has the opposite \(y\)-coordinate. Hence \(\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta\); sine is an odd function.
questions.hint: Reflecting a point in the \(x\)-axis changes the sign of one coordinate.

questions.learningObjective: Derive the identity for the tangent of a negative angle.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\tan(-\theta)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Using the quotient identity, \(\tan(-\theta)=\frac{\sin(-\theta)}{\cos(-\theta)}=\frac{-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=-\tan\theta\). An odd function divided by an even function is odd.
questions.hint: Write tangent as sine over cosine and apply the identities for \(\sin(-\theta)\) and \(\cos(-\theta)\).

questions.concept: Sine of a negative standard angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sine at a negative angle using the odd identity.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\sin(-30^\circ)\)?
questions.explanation: Sine is odd, so \(\sin(-30^\circ)=-\sin 30^\circ=-\frac{1}{2}\). The angle \(-30^\circ\) is in Quadrant IV, where the \(y\)-coordinate is negative, which confirms the sign.

questions.concept: Cosine of a negative standard angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a cosine at a negative angle using the even identity.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: Cosine is even, so \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{2}\). The angle \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) is in Quadrant IV, where the \(x\)-coordinate is positive.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether secant is even or odd from the parity of cosine.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\sec(-\theta)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Since \(\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\) and cosine is even, \(\sec(-\theta)=\frac{1}{\cos(-\theta)}=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=\sec\theta\). A reciprocal has the same parity as the original function, so secant is even.
questions.hint: Write secant as a reciprocal and use the parity of cosine.

questions.concept: Product of sine and cosine at a negative angle
questions.learningObjective: Simplify a product using both the even and odd identities.
questions.question: For every angle \(\theta\), \(\sin(-\theta)\cos(-\theta)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Apply the identities separately: \(\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta\) and \(\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta\). The product is \((-\sin\theta)(\cos\theta)=-\sin\theta\cos\theta\). Only one of the two factors changes sign.
questions.hint: Only the odd function changes sign when the angle is negated.

questions.concept: Tangent of a negative standard angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a tangent at a negative angle using the odd identity.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: Tangent is odd, so \(\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\tan\frac{\pi}{4}=-1\). The angle \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\) is in Quadrant IV, where sine and cosine have opposite signs.

questions.concept: Simplifying a sum with a negative angle
questions.learningObjective: Simplify an expression that mixes a negative-angle quotient with a tangent.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\frac{\sin(-\theta)}{\cos(-\theta)}+\tan\theta\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: The fraction is \(\frac{-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=-\tan\theta\). Adding \(\tan\theta\) gives \(-\tan\theta+\tan\theta=0\). The value \(-2\tan\theta\) would result from subtracting \(\tan\theta\) instead of adding it.
questions.hint: Simplify the fraction first using the even and odd identities.

questions.learningObjective: Classify a function built from an odd polynomial factor and sine as even or odd.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=x\sin x\) for all real \(x\). Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Compute \(f(-x)=(-x)\sin(-x)=(-x)(-\sin x)=x\sin x=f(x)\). Both factors change sign, and the two sign changes cancel, so \(f\) is even. A product of two odd functions is even, not odd.
questions.hint: Replace \(x\) by \(-x\) in both factors and count the sign changes.
